items.title: Framed link diagrams and local Reidemeister moves in plane products
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal A$ be a compact smooth
planar annulus and set
$X=\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)\times(-1,1)
=\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])$, the interior of a solid torus.
A regular annular diagram is a finite immersed union of circles in
$\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)$ with only finitely many transverse double
points, no triple points, and over/under data from the interval coordinate.
The **blackboard framing** is the normal strip lying in the annulus. A specified
framing differs from it on each component by an integer full-twist correction,
measured by the winding number of its normal direction relative to the
blackboard normal. Count the correction positively for an A-type full twist,
whose local curl has A-smoothing equal to the straight strip with one
contractible circle; count the opposite B-type twist negatively. Every framed
link in $X$ admits a regular annular diagram. The correction may be recorded
as signed full-twist marks on diagram arcs; its total is additive when arcs
are concatenated.

If two framed links in $X$ are ambient isotopic through links in $X$, their
regular annular diagrams are related by finitely many annular planar isotopies
and local oriented Reidemeister I, II, and III moves in disks contained in
$\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)$. Reidemeister II and III and planar isotopy
preserve the blackboard framing; an A-type or B-type Reidemeister I move
changes it by one corresponding full twist, so the correction integer changes
by the opposite twist. For framed links in $S^3$, every link also admits a
regular planar diagram, and any two diagrams of ambient-isotopic framed links
are related by a finite planar-isotopy/Reidemeister sequence with the same
framing-correction rule.
items.strategy: Put link and isotopy projections in general position; use the local cusp, tangency, and triple-event models, then track the blackboard framing through each move.

references.title: Józef H. Przytycki, Fundamentals of Kauffman Bracket Skein Modules, arXiv:math/9809113 (1998), §3, Lemma 3.5 and Proposition 3.6
Daniel Queffelec, Reidemeister's theorem using transversality, arXiv:2406.18203v1 (2024), §§2–3.6

items.axiom_use: Assumes ACω only for the cited generic-position and oriented Reidemeister results. Finite-jet perturbations, local framing tracking, and the skein calculations are choice-free.

items.title: Kauffman bracket skein module of a three-manifold
items.strategy: Defines the free module and the submodule generated by the two local bracket relations using the KT-29 crossing convention.

references.title: Józef H. Przytycki, Fundamentals of Kauffman Bracket Skein Modules, arXiv:math/9809113 (1998), §2, Definition 2.1
Sean Pohorence, 3-manifold Invariants and TQFTs (January 2016), §3.1, Definition 3.1.1, pp. 11–12
Thang T. Q. Le, A Crash Course in Quantum Invariants of Knots and 3-Manifolds (2016), §6.1, p. 29

items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the free module is the finitely supported formal R-linear combinations of a set of framed-link isotopy classes, and the quotient is by the explicitly generated relation submodule.

items.title: Full framing twists in the Kauffman bracket skein module
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth oriented $3$-manifold and let $L$ be a framed unoriented
link in its interior with a specified component. A positive full framing twist is the local blackboard
curl whose $A$-smoothing is the straight strip with one additional
zero-framed trivial circle; a negative full framing twist is the curl whose
$B$-smoothing is the straight strip with one additional zero-framed trivial
circle. Write $L^+$ and $L^-$ for the links obtained by inserting these twists
on one component. With $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$ and
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$, the module classes satisfy
$$
[L^+]=-A^3[L],\qquad [L^-]=-A^{-3}[L].
$$
items.strategy: Resolve the positive and negative blackboard curls and use the trivial-circle relation with δ=−A²−A⁻².

references.title: Józef H. Przytycki, Fundamentals of Kauffman Bracket Skein Modules, arXiv:math/9809113 (1998), §2, framing relation following Definition 2.1
Thang T. Q. Le, A Crash Course in Quantum Invariants of Knots and 3-Manifolds (2016), §6.1

items.axiom_use: Choice-free: both twist factors follow from one local skein expansion and the trivial-circle relation.

items.title: Functoriality and boundary-collar action for the three-manifold skein quotient
items.statement:
Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth oriented $3$-manifolds, and let
$f:M\to N$ be an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism. Then
$[L]\mapsto[f(L)]$ induces an $R$-module isomorphism
$f_*:\mathcal K_A(M)\to\mathcal K_A(N)$. These maps respect identity
diffeomorphisms and composition.

Let $\Sigma$ be a compact oriented surface with a specified product collar
$\iota:\Sigma\times[0,1]\hookrightarrow M$ whose lower face lies in
$\partial M$. Give $\Sigma\times[0,1]$ the orientation pulled back from $M$
by $\iota$; the skein module and stacking product below use this orientation.
The stacking product on
$\mathcal K_A(\Sigma\times[0,1])$ and collar gluing define a unital left
action on $\mathcal K_A(M)$: a closed framed link in the surface product is
placed in a sufficiently thin outer subcollar and united with a framed link
in the interior of $M$. The action is independent of the thin-collar width,
associative, and natural under orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms that
respect the specified collars. Only closed framed links are glued; no relative
boundary endpoints are part of this action.
items.strategy: Push each local relation through the diffeomorphism or collar embedding, then verify inverse, composition, unit, and associativity from the corresponding geometric operations.

references.title: Józef H. Przytycki, Fundamentals of Kauffman Bracket Skein Modules, arXiv:math/9809113 (1998), §2, Proposition 2.2(i)
Sean Pohorence, 3-manifold Invariants and TQFTs (January 2016), §§1.2 and 3.1
Thang T. Q. Le, A Crash Course in Quantum Invariants of Knots and 3-Manifolds (2016), §6.1, pp. 29–30

items.axiom_use: Choice-free: a diffeomorphism, collar embedding, and gluing operation act canonically on link representatives and carry each displayed local relation to the same relation.

items.title: Kauffman bracket evaluation of framed links in the three-sphere
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and let $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$ and
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. For a nonempty framed unoriented link $L$ in $S^3$,
choose a regular planar diagram $D$ of its core. Let $m_j\in\mathbb Z$ be
the full-twist correction on the $j$th component from the blackboard framing
of $D$ to the specified framing of $L$, counting an A-type twist positively
and its inverse negatively as in the framed diagram calculus, and put
$m=\sum_jm_j$. For a state
$S$ of $D$, let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ be its numbers of A- and B-smoothings and
$|S|$ its number of resulting circles. The assignment
$$E(\varnothing)=1,\qquad E(L)=\delta(-A^3)^m\sum_{S}A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{|S|-1}$$
is independent of the diagram and twist corrections and extends
$R$-linearly to a map $E:\mathcal K_A(S^3)\to R$ satisfying
$E([\varnothing])=1$.
items.strategy: Use framed Reidemeister moves to prove diagram independence; partition states at a crossing and add a trivial circle to verify the two skein relations.

references.title: Józef H. Przytycki, Fundamentals of Kauffman Bracket Skein Modules, arXiv:math/9809113 (1998), §2, Theorem 2.3(a)
Sean Pohorence, 3-manifold Invariants and TQFTs (January 2016), §3.1, pp. 11–12
Thang T. Q. Le, A Crash Course in Quantum Invariants of Knots and 3-Manifolds (2016), §6.2, Example 6.4, p. 30

items.axiom_use: Assumes ACω only through framed diagram equivalence; state expansion and module-relation checks are choice-free.

items.title: Annular state expansion for the Kauffman bracket skein module
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal A$ be a planar annulus
and identify the solid torus with $\mathcal A\times[-1,1]$. Let
$R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$, $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$, and let $z$ be a formal
polynomial variable. For a regular annular diagram $D$, a state $S$ smooths
every crossing. Let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ count its A- and B-smoothings, let
$u(S)$ count the resulting circles that bound disks in $\mathcal A$, and let
$e(S)$ count the resulting circles that do not bound disks in $\mathcal A$;
call a circle that does not bound a disk essential.
If $m$ is the total full-twist correction from the blackboard framing to the
specified framing, counting an A-type twist positively and its inverse
negatively as in the framed diagram calculus, set
$$
\Psi(D,m)=(-A^3)^m\sum_S A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{u(S)}z^{e(S)}.
$$
This value is independent of the regular annular diagram and twist correction
of the framed link and induces an $R$-linear map
$$
\Psi:\mathcal K_A(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])\longrightarrow R[z].
$$
For the empty link, the empty diagram has its unique empty state and the
formula gives $\Psi(\varnothing)=1$.

The diagram below shows one essential core curve and one contractible circle
in an annular state; every smoothed component is classified by these two
types.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.75,line cap=round]
  \draw[thick] (0,0) circle (1.6);
  \draw[thick] (0,0) circle (0.65);
  \draw[very thick] (0,0) circle (1.05);
  \draw[very thick] (1.30,0) circle (0.16);
  \node at (0,1.05) [above] {$z$};
  \node at (1.45,0.25) [right] {$\bigcirc$};
  \node at (0,-1.95) {essential core and contractible circle};
\end{tikzpicture}
```
items.strategy: Resolve each crossing, evaluate contractible circles by δ and essential annular circles by z, then verify move, framing, crossing, and trivial-circle compatibility.

references.title: Józef H. Przytycki, Fundamentals of Kauffman Bracket Skein Modules, arXiv:math/9809113 (1998), §3, Lemmas 3.3 and 3.5
Sean Pohorence, 3-manifold Invariants and TQFTs (January 2016), §3.1, pp. 11–12
Thang T. Q. Le, A Crash Course in Quantum Invariants of Knots and 3-Manifolds (2016), §6.2, Proposition 6.2 and Example 6.5, pp. 29–30

items.axiom_use: Assumes full AC for the annular state-circle classification and ACω through the annular framed-diagram calculus; the state expansion and local Temperley–Lieb calculations add no choice.

items.title: The Kauffman bracket skein module of S³ is rank one
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and let $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$ and
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. The Kauffman bracket skein module
$\mathcal K_A(S^3)$ is freely generated as an $R$-module by the empty link.
In particular, a zero-framed trivial circle represents
$\delta[\varnothing]$.
items.strategy: Resolve every crossing to a finite combination of unlinks for spanning, and use the framed bracket evaluation with empty value one to prove the empty class is nonzero and independent.

references.title: Józef H. Przytycki, Fundamentals of Kauffman Bracket Skein Modules, arXiv:math/9809113 (1998), §2, Theorem 2.3(a)
Sean Pohorence, 3-manifold Invariants and TQFTs (January 2016), §3.1, pp. 11–12
Thang T. Q. Le, A Crash Course in Quantum Invariants of Knots and 3-Manifolds (2016), §6.2, Example 6.4, p. 30

items.axiom_use: Assumes ACω only through the framed-diagram existence and equivalence supplier. State resolution, framing reduction, and the module argument are choice-free.

items.title: The solid-torus skein module has a core-multicurve basis
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$. Identify
the solid torus with $\mathcal A\times[-1,1]$, where $\mathcal A$ is a planar
annulus. A simple closed curve is called essential if it does not bound a disk
in $\mathcal A$. Every framed link in this product admits a regular annular
diagram and an integer framing correction from its blackboard framing. Let
$z$ be one blackboard-framed annular core curve, and for $n\geq1$ let $z^n$
denote $n$ parallel copies of that curve, with $z^0$ the empty link. In the polynomial
ring $R[z]$, $z$ is also the formal variable sent to the core class $[z]$.
Then the classes $[z^n]$, $n\geq0$, form an $R$-basis of
$\mathcal K_A(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])$. Equivalently, the map
$J:R[z]\to\mathcal K_A(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])$ sending $z^n$ to $[z^n]$ is
an $R$-module isomorphism.
items.strategy: Use the annular state expansion as a two-sided inverse to the map from polynomial monomials to parallel core multicurves; crossing resolution gives spanning and the polynomial monomials give independence.

references.title: Józef H. Przytycki, Fundamentals of Kauffman Bracket Skein Modules, arXiv:math/9809113 (1998), §3, Theorem 3.1 and proof
Sean Pohorence, 3-manifold Invariants and TQFTs (January 2016), §3.1, pp. 11–12
Thang T. Q. Le, A Crash Course in Quantum Invariants of Knots and 3-Manifolds (2016), §6.2, Proposition 6.2 and Example 6.5, pp. 29–30

items.axiom_use: Assumes full AC through the annular state-circle classification; ACω enters through framed diagram existence. The state-map inverse and module argument add no choice.

items.title: Skein-module isomorphisms preserve framings and boundary actions
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. An orientation-preserving diffeomorphism
between smooth oriented $3$-manifolds transports the full framing of every
link and induces an isomorphism of their Kauffman bracket skein modules. If
the diffeomorphism carries a specified product collar of a compact oriented
boundary surface productwise to another specified collar, the induced
isomorphism intertwines the two closed-link collar actions. A positive or
negative full framing twist on one link component multiplies its class by
$-A^3$ or $-A^{-3}$, respectively. In $\mathcal K_A(S^3)$, a positive twist
of a zero-framed trivial circle changes its class from
$\delta[\varnothing]$ to $-A^3\delta[\varnothing]$, with
$\delta[\varnothing]\ne -A^3\delta[\varnothing]$. In the solid-torus
module, a positive twist of the blackboard-framed core changes $[z]$ to
$-A^3[z]$, with $[z]\ne -A^3[z]$.
items.strategy: Combine functoriality and collar gluing with the local framing-twist calculation, then use the S³ and solid-torus bases to verify that the stated framing changes are nontrivial.

references.title: Józef H. Przytycki, Fundamentals of Kauffman Bracket Skein Modules, arXiv:math/9809113 (1998), §2, Proposition 2.2(i), and §3, Theorem 3.1
Sean Pohorence, 3-manifold Invariants and TQFTs (January 2016), §3.1, pp. 11–12
Thang T. Q. Le, A Crash Course in Quantum Invariants of Knots and 3-Manifolds (2016), §6.1, pp. 29–30

items.axiom_use: The quotient functor, collar action, and twist scalar are choice-free. Full AC supplies the solid-torus basis; its countable consequence supplies the S3 basis.

title: Skein modules for links in 3-manifolds — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Forgetting framing identifies distinct skein classes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$. The
assertion that the Kauffman bracket skein module can be formed from unframed
link-isotopy classes without changing its classes is false. In $S^3$, a
zero-framed trivial circle and the same circle with one positive full framing
twist have distinct skein classes. In a solid torus, a zero-framed core and
the same core with one positive full framing twist also have distinct skein
classes. In each pair the underlying unframed embedded link is identical.
items.strategy: Use the framing-twist scalar and the free S³ and solid-torus basis descriptions to exhibit two unequal classes in each manifold.

references.title: Józef H. Przytycki, Fundamentals of Kauffman Bracket Skein Modules, arXiv:math/9809113 (1998), §2, framing relation and Theorem 2.3(a)
Sean Pohorence, 3-manifold Invariants and TQFTs (January 2016), §3.1, pp. 11–12

items.axiom_use: Assumes full AC for the solid-torus basis and its countable consequence for the S3 basis.

items.title: The empty link, trivial circle, and annular core multicurves
items.strategy: Evaluate the trivial circle by its defining relation, distinguish z and z² by the core-multicurve basis, and identify the collar action by the gluing construction.
